items.title: Wayne Andre interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002
items.q: Benny called Lou Schoobe who was the contractor at CBS to find out if I could get a break from the Gary Moore Show

ctx.x: Well I know he didn’t make a lot of friends on that trip. I’ve talked to some of the guys who were on that tour.

Well yeah. I don’t think there’s anybody in the band that was certainly — you know ironically if anybody in that band, and I’m thinking about everybody in the band now, if anybody had something nice to say about Benny and not dark and negative, it was Teddy Wilson. Teddy Wilson wasn’t getting to play at all and — hardly at all — and he was as mild in manner, he was a gentleman. I mean this is like, Teddy Wilson was a first class cat man. And I don’t know, there are certain things that could have been better on…

my cap I guess but this is what was told to me, I mean it was told to me by the contractor at CBS, not by Benny, that Benny went to Paley, William Paley. He went to the CEO, and said I want this guy and tell the contractor to let him go. So I mean it makes me feel good that somebody wanted me that much to go through all that trouble. And so that made me feel good. So from that standpoint it’s hard to badmouth someone — but anyways, so I went. And some kid that was playing third trombone, he was a teacher and I…
